data.name: Partha
data.gender_notes: Partha is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Partha is derived from the Sanskrit word 'partha' which means 'Son of Arjuna'. Partha is an epithet for Arjuna, one of the greatest warriors in Hindu mythology, and is often referred to as Bhishma-partha or Arjuna-partha. Partha is also associated with the god Krishna, who is believed to have appeared before Arjuna in his divine form, and is known as Parthasarathi, or the charioteer of Arjuna.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the inner warrior, courage, and victory over one's inner demons and external challenges.
data.etymology: Partha belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Son of Arjuna.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Partha total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: Partha carries the legacy of Arjuna, one of the most revered warriors in Hindu literature. It symbolizes courage, wisdom, and unwavering devotion to duty. Arjuna, represented by the name Partha, was known for his skill and strength both on the battlefield and in spiritual pursuits. The name reminds us of the traditional Hindu values of dharma (duty), artha (prosperity), kama (desire), and moksha (liberation), which were upheld by Arjuna. It is an inspiring name for those who seek to embody the qualities of a great leader and warrior.
data.spiritual_significance: Partha also has deep spiritual significance as it signifies the divine bond between Krishna and Arjuna. The name is a reminder of the timeless teachings of the Bhagavad Gita, which was revealed to Arjuna by Krishna during the Mahabharata war. Parthasarathi, or Krishna as the charioteer of Arjuna, is an embodiment of divine guidance and the essence of the guru-disciple relationship. Partha symbolizes the journey of self-discovery and spiritual growth, and those who bear this name are believed to possess the strength, determination, and wisdom to fulfill their dharma and ultimately attain moksha.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Partha, meaning "son of Arjuna" in Sanskrit, symbolizes the journey of the devoted soul under the guidance of a wise mentor towards self-realization and dharma (duty or righteousness).

historical_references.context: Partha is the pre-coronation name of Arjuna, one of the five Pandava brothers.

historical_references.reference: Buddhist Jataka Tales - A collection of 547 stories of the Buddha's former lives, retold to illustrate moral lessons.
historical_references.context: Partha is the name of a prince who, in one of these tales, performs selfless acts to save his father's life.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Partha continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
